headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: Airflow can feed Pipecat shared text/state, while Pipecat’s shared bus and outbound model/API calls amplify bad inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can move files and API outputs into downstream tasks, and Pipecat consumes text/conversation state over a shared bus. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Airflow-produced content is treated as trusted input by Pipecat. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is forwarded into Pipecat text or conversation state without sanitization
IF Pipecat parses shared-bus content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist schema for Airflow-to-Pipecat messages
Strip control tokens and prompt-like prefixes before handoff
Route only structured JSON, not free text
Log and review first 10 cross-agent messages
requires-engineering: add provenance tags on every shared-bus payload

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and Pipecat touches text, audio, video, images, and conversation state with allowlisted outbound calls. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive artifacts can flow from Airflow into Pipecat and then out to third-party services. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Airflow and Pipecat share a workspace, bus, or mounted volume
IF Pipecat is configured to send received text/audio to external STT/LLM/TTS providers
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable external providers in Pipecat for sensitive runs
Pass only redacted fields from Airflow
Rotate any secrets exposed in shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-message data-class labels

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is a data-engineering orchestrator with broad egress, while Pipecat supports shared-bus concurrency and multiple instances. Their write surfaces are not documented as overlapping on the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is not established. The main risk is coordination friction, not destructive contention.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external resource without locking
IF the orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable queue or file
mitigations: Assign separate queues or topics
Use per-agent output directories
Add a lock around shared writes
Monitor for duplicate writes
requires-engineering: introduce optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate and route outputs that Pipecat may treat as conversation state or text, and Pipecat can then call external LLM/STT/TTS services. That makes a bad upstream artifact capable of cascading into downstream actions or user-facing responses. Because the pairwise verification is indirect, uncertainty does not reduce the severity below high.
conditions: IF Pipecat consumes Airflow output without a verification step
IF Pipecat forwards that output into downstream model calls or user-facing speech
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before Pipecat acts on Airflow output
Require checksum or schema validation on handoff
Limit Pipecat to read-only summarization for Airflow data
Add rollback for any downstream side effects
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention obligations are documented in either profile, and both are open/source-available with docs-only evidence. The only compliance concern is generic policy mismatch if Airflow-managed data is later sent by Pipecat to third-party providers. That is plausible but not established, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Airflow into Pipecat
IF Pipecat is configured to use third-party STT/LLM/TTS services for that data
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Block regulated fields from Pipecat providers
Document retention settings for each provider
Review vendor DPAs before enabling external APIs
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
